correctness.rationale: Exact two-period product is (J P_c(d) D_1)^2. The fixed diagonal similarity to symmetric S(d) yields a closed formula; strict convexity follows from noncollinear affine vectors (c(B-b)d,2 sqrt(Bb)(1-d)). Endpoints are sqrt(Bb) and cB, giving all optimizers including equality. Differentiated curvature proves the uniform positive penalty. Exact rational independent script checks the matrix reduction and a threshold witness; no finite experiment is used to infer universal validity.

originality.rationale: The main primary full-text dispersal theorem (Schreiber and Li 2010) explicitly excludes migration mortality and notes costs as an unresolved analytical challenge; the exact c<1 phase boundary and strict interior-loss statement are not supplied by its no-cost results. The older two-patch density-regulated article expressly assumes no deaths in dispersal. Searches of aliases and relevant indexed claims found no equivalent closed-form classification. Bibliographic uncertainty from partly inaccessible related papers remains documented.

value.rationale: Provides a complete sharp optimizer classification of a natural, exactly alternating two-patch ecological growth model with mortality during movement, including the discontinuous travel-survival boundary and explicit nonzero penalty for every partial strategy. This addresses the ecologically motivated cost question explicitly raised in the primary period-two literature rather than a merely renamed computation. It is useful as a rigorous benchmark, without overclaiming applicability to stochastic or density-regulated ecosystems.
